_comment: A deep cavalry squadron wheels onto an enemy in contact instead of swinging its ranks round under its men. A 60-horse Cavalry squadron (team 0, 8 files on 40 wu by 8 ranks on 120 wu, its corner about 443 wu from its anchor) stands facing north on Hold. A 30-man Infantry block (team 1, the enemy AI) spawns facing south just north-east of its anchor and attacks it, coming into contact at tick 147 with its centre about 45 degrees east of the squadron's heading. That is a small re-face (under the 75 degree threshold past which the men turn in place), and on main 766cd5ed it snapped the heading 45.4 degrees in one tick, turning the whole slot grid about the anchor with it: at tick 152, 23 of the 60 riders had their slot across the centreline from them and the farthest slot lay 282.1 wu sideways of its rider, while the riders, held in the fight, stayed where they stood; the squadron fell out of contact as its grid swung away, re-faced again each time it came back, and by tick 360 its grid stood 118.6 degrees off its riders at the best fit, its farthest rider 880.6 wu from his slot. Now the squadron wheels its heading and grid together onto the infantry no faster than its corner riders can jog (70 wu/s, about 1.17 wu a tick at the corner), and fights on while it does (Unit._wheel_combat_reface): at tick 152 no slot is across the centreline and the farthest lies 8.1 wu sideways of its rider, at tick 200 only 3 are across, and it stays in contact through tick 360 with its grid never more than 10.4 degrees off its riders at the best fit. The tolerance on the tick-152 excess (12 wu) is 5 ticks of the corner's jog sweep since contact (5.8 wu) plus about 6 wu for riders already a little off their slots. Static camera. Deterministic (scenario + seed + scripted input). Measured with 2-tick FULL state dumps on main 766cd5ed and on this branch.
